1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier 与 regio: 1) Take db_instance_identifier and region from the alert labels and sort by Top SQL in Performance Insights to find the statements burning the most CPU; 2) Run EXPLAIN on the statements you find; a full scan from a missing index is the most common cause; 3) Confirm no unusual batch jobs or analytical queries are hitting the primary, and move them to a read replica if they are; 4) Only after optimisation should you upgrade the instance class, and that change must be made inside a maintenance window.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，先确认是否开启: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and first check whether Multi-AZ is enabled, since synchronous replication makes write latency higher than a single-AZ instance and that is expected; 2) Compare WriteIOPS against the volume's IOPS ceiling and handle saturation via the burst balance / storage type path; 3) Check whether a large transaction or bulk import is running; splitting it into smaller batches reduces latency substantially; 4) If binlog/WAL write amplification is obvious, confirm sync_binlog and innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit actually match the durability the business requires.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，同时看 Rea: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and look at ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS together with BurstBalance to see whether the IOPS ceiling has been reached; 2) Sort by IO wait in Performance Insights to find the SQL generating the IO and optimise those statements first; 3) Confirm that backups, snapshots, and index rebuilds do not overlap the business peak; 4) If the workload genuinely needs more IOPS, switch to gp3 and set IOPS and throughput explicitly.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，在 Cloud: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and compare ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS in CloudWatch against the volume's baseline IOPS to size the overrun; 2) Reduce IO at the source first: use Performance Insights to find the queries with the most physical reads and add indexes; 3) As an emergency measure switch the storage type to gp3 or io1/io2 for guaranteed IOPS; the gp3 change can be made online; 4) Growing the volume also raises baseline IOPS, but is usually less cost-effective than moving to gp3.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，在 Perfo: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and review the memory-related wait events in Performance Insights; 2) Check whether innodb_buffer_pool_size (MySQL) or shared_buffers (PostgreSQL) in the parameter group is set too large; anything above 75% of instance memory tends to trigger this; 3) Excessive connections also consume memory: confirm the application uses a connection pool and that max_connections is not far above what you actually need; 4) Only once the configuration is sane should you move to an instance class with more memory.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，在控制台确认当: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and confirm the allocated and used capacity in the console; 2) Expand storage immediately (Modify > Allocated storage); RDS scaling is online but has a 6-hour cooldown, so do not wait until it is full; 3) At the same time reclaim space: drop stale temporary tables, shorten binlog retention (call mysql.rds_set_configuration('binlog retention hours', N)), and archive historical partitions; 4) Longer term enable Storage Autoscaling with a sensible upper bound.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，对比同时段的: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and compare ReadIOPS and BurstBalance for the same period to rule out an exhausted IO burst balance first; 2) If IOPS are not saturated but latency is high, check whether a large scan is flushing the buffer pool and use Performance Insights to find the SQL with the most physical reads; 3) Adding indexes to cut physical reads is the most effective fix, followed by moving analytical queries to a read replica; 4) If the workload is reasonable and latency is still high, upgrade the storage type to gp3/io1 for more predictable latency.
1) 从告警标签取 db_instance_identifier，结合 Free: 1) Take db_instance_identifier from the alert labels and read it together with FreeableMemory to see how long the memory pressure has lasted; 2) Check whether the buffer pool parameters in the parameter group are set too large and whether the connection count exceeds expectations; 3) Look for large sorts or large temporary tables consuming memory, locate them in Performance Insights, and optimise them; 4) If configuration and queries are both reasonable and swapping continues, move to an instance class with more memory.
RDS 实例 CPU 使用率持续超过 85%，查询会开始排队，响应时间上升，突发: RDS instance CPU utilization has stayed above 85%. Queries start queuing, response times rise, and a traffic burst could make it unavailable.
RDS 实例 CPU 使用率过高: RDS instance CPU utilization too high
RDS 实例 IO 突发余额耗尽: RDS instance IO burst balance low
RDS 实例 Swap 使用超过 256MB，说明物理内存已经不够用，数据库开始: The RDS instance is using more than 256 MB of swap, which means physical memory is no longer sufficient and the database has started swapping. Query latency will rise noticeably and unpredictably.
RDS 实例 Swap 使用过高: RDS instance swap usage too high
RDS 实例写延迟过高: RDS instance write latency too high
RDS 实例可用存储空间不足: RDS instance free storage space low
RDS 实例可用存储空间已不足 10GB，写满后实例会进入 storage-fu: The RDS instance has less than 10 GB of free storage. Once it fills, the instance enters the storage-full state, all writes fail, and it cannot recover on its own.
RDS 实例可释放内存已不足 512MB，缓冲池会开始换出，物理读激增，严重时实: The RDS instance has less than 512 MB of freeable memory. The buffer pool starts evicting pages, physical reads spike, and in severe cases the instance restarts from memory exhaustion.
RDS 实例平均写延迟超过 50 毫秒（CloudWatch WriteLate: The RDS instance's average write latency exceeds 50 ms (the CloudWatch WriteLatency metric is in seconds). Transaction commits are slowed and overall write throughput drops.
RDS 实例平均读延迟超过 50 毫秒（CloudWatch ReadLaten: The RDS instance's average read latency exceeds 50 ms (the CloudWatch ReadLatency metric is in seconds). Storage has become the bottleneck and query response times will grow noticeably.
RDS 实例磁盘队列深度持续超过 10，说明 IO 请求排队严重，存储已经跟不上: The RDS instance's disk queue depth has stayed above 10, meaning IO requests are queuing badly and storage can no longer keep up. Every query is slowed as a result.
RDS 实例磁盘队列积压: RDS instance disk queue backing up
RDS 实例读延迟过高: RDS instance read latency too high
gp2 卷的 IO 突发余额已低于 20%，耗尽后 IOPS 会跌回基线水平（每: The gp2 volume's IO burst balance has fallen below 20%. Once exhausted, IOPS drop back to the baseline (3 IOPS per GB) and database performance falls off a cliff.
